new_statements.rule_in_words: Icen is analysed with four level tones (Top, High, Mid, Low) plus two falling tones (High-to-Low, Top-to-Low); syllable (C1)(C2)(C3)V; the comparative chapter repeats that Icen (with Kutep) has four level tones against Proto-Jukunoid's three. Nothing about word stress was visible.
new_statements.identity_note: The snippet carries the section heading '1.1.4 ICEN (Icen)' and the running footer '-72- Icen'; Shimizu's Icen is the Kpan-Icen (Central Jukunoid) language = Etkywan [ich] (Glottolog cites this work as the Glottolog's most extensive description for etky1238; BCCW 1973 equates 'Kentu (Kyato) (= Icen)'). Not Kpan/Kente (treated separately by Shimizu as 'Kpan Knte').

sources.note: Nothing on Ichen prosody. The only tone remarks (p. 356) compare Wapan with Kuteb and Etulo ('Kokwi High-Mid tone in Wapan and Kaensi High-Mid tone in Kuteb', 'both having mid-tones at the final position of the word'); the Ichen column in Table 1 is written without tone marks. Also relays Meek (1931, cited as 1930:121) that Ichen/Chamba, Kona, Gwana and Pindiga use nominal suffixes where Wapan uses the prefix a- (morphology, not prosody).
